text:
Filip Forsberg is 32, has played every one of his 885 NHL games in Nashville, and is having a good, not great, season: 9 goals and 25 points in 23 games, with 62 shots. The Predators ran off a long winning streak in early November, and his heavy shot (top speed in the 92nd percentile) is still the best thing about his game.

The points are padded, though. Nashville has scored 11.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, while his own finishing (14.5%) sits right where it should. His team takes 51% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, even as it loses the shot-attempt battle. Last season ran the other way: Evolving-Hockey said he was worth 2.5 expected wins by chance quality against 0.9 actual, so the luck is finally on his side. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found nothing far from a typical forward last season. He scored 40 goals last year, and our numbers see 28 to 44 this time. That on-ice luck is the part our numbers expect to fade.
headline: Forsberg's points are outrunning Nashville's chances
